question: A customer data center is configured for distribution of user roles, call home, and NTP. The data center was split into two geographically separate locations called DC1 and DC2. The requirement is for the user role configurations to be distributed in DC1 and for NTP and call home features to be constrained to DC2. Which two configuration sets must be used to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options:
! On Data Center 1
configure terminal
cfs region 1
 roles
 aaa

! On Data Center 1
configure terminal
cfs region 1
 ntp
 callhome

! On Data Center 1
configure terminal
cfs region 1
 ntp
 callhome

! On Data Center 2
configure terminal
cfs region 2
 roles

! On Data Center 2
configure terminal
cfs region 2
 roles
 aaa
theory: Cisco Fabric Services (CFS) is the peer-to-peer infrastructure NX-OS uses to automatically synchronize application configuration across switches in a fabric, and its distribution scope can be scoped to a defined "CFS region" so that only switches in that region share a given application's config. Since user roles/AAA need to synchronize within DC1 and NTP/Call Home need to synchronize within DC2, each site defines its own CFS region (e.g., region 1 for DC1, region 2 for DC2) and lists only the CFS-enabled applications (roles/aaa vs. ntp/callhome) that should be distributed within that region. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 — Cisco Fabric Services)
